Shrinking of the Core (Debreu–Scarf)

Copy the same economy and grow its scale. Watch the divisions everyone accepts narrow down to one.

When the economy is small, a few agents can break away and do better alone. As 🧑 people multiply, those escape routes get sliced away. Exactly one division survives in the end. It is the very division the market picks. The core shrinks to a point, as in the formula below.

For example, splitting 10 🍎 apples between 2 friends, almost any split works. Grow the group to 100 friends and the story changes. Unhappy friends can team up and cook up a new split. In the end only one split survives — one nobody can break away from.

core(N)↓{x∗}(N→∞)\text{core}(N) \downarrow \{x^*\} \quad (N \to \infty)core(N)↓{x∗}(N→∞)

Part of these learning paths

  • General Equilibrium and Welfare
